title: Catholic Ashrams: Sannyasins or Swindlers?
byline: by Sita Ram Goel, with articles from Hinduism Today · Voice of India · 1988, enlarged in the 1990s
lede: Catholic monks in saffron, with Sanskrit chants, temple-style chapels and an Om on the cross. Goel argues these ashrams are not dialogue but a missionary method the Church calls indigenisation or inculturation. He traces it from the Jesuit Robert De Nobili, who posed as a Brahmin sannyasi in 17th-century Madurai, to Bede Griffiths at Shantivanam. He sets out his case through Griffiths' own letters.
facts: chapters, plus appendices on ashrams, mission money and missionary statistics
Christian ashrams listed: 108 in India, 4 in Nepal and 8 in Sri Lanka (as of 1988)

the Saccidananda Ashram at Tannirpalli is founded
note: Goel writes as an opponent of Christian missions, and his title asks a loaded question. The book reprints both sides of several exchanges, including Bede Griffiths' own letters. This page summarises Goel's argument and the documents, attributed to their authors.
